item.title: Memory-efficient JSON in .NET 10 web APIs with PipeReader
item.description: Deserializing a JSON payload with a million objects strains memory and the garbage collector. .NET 10 adds PipeReader support to System.Text.Json, letting the serializer read straight from a pipeline. This post benchmarks it against streams on execution time, allocations, and GC collections. Worth a read for developers following .NET and DevOps. Link to article: https://blog.elmah.io/memory-efficient-json-in-net-10-web-apis-with-pipereader

item.title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM
item.description: vLLM's prefill-decode disaggregation splits LLM inference across engine instances but must transfer the KV cache between them. This post introduces a push-based NIXL connector that moves transfer coordination off the critical path, delivering up to 3x better TTFT and 30% better TPOT in benchmarks on Amazon EC2 P5en instances with AWS EFA. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/push-based-kv-transfer-to-improve-ttft-and-tpot-for-disaggregated-inference-in-vllm

item.title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock. In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three reasoning tasks at four reasoning effort levels, measuring correctness and token cost per completed task. We show how to tune the trade-off per request and monitor it in production. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/build-long-horizon-agents-with-grok-4-7-on-amazon-bedrock

item.title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: AWS engineers share kernel optimizations for fused Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on Amazon SageMaker AI: Swap-AB for WGMMA utilization, Triton backend routing for FP8 quantization, and eliminating Triton JIT recompilation. Together they deliver up to 10% higher throughput and up to 9% faster Time to First Token on H200 GPUs. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/mixture-of-experts-kernel-engineering-on-amazon-sagemaker-ai
